title: Tulsa musicians: Oscar Estelle, Elon Watkins and Thomas Ross
summary: Tulsa's high-school band tradition produced West and Bostic; Fields remembers trumpeter-writer Thomas Ross, who wrote Thursday Evening Blues.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Usually now one guy--but you need more than just one man, I think Oscar Estelle was in the band, that's why we did finally make it and talking about Tulsa, you take Spurgeon, Earl Bostic, came up through high school under William Jett and they would always find the little bandstand out of the military band; then my brother came--the one that I was telling you when I first came out of school in Sand Springs, he moved into Tulsa and was a band director of high school, and really, Clarence Little was one guy that used to work on that little dance that they had. (Inaudible).
Oscar and Elon Watkins and I believe it was Thomas Ross, he's a trumpet player, he never did get to make it, he got into bad health, drinking, but was a very fine
musician--Thomas Ross--and he was a nice writer too. I think I have one of the old pictures that he was in.
One number was his--Thursday Evening Blues--that used to feature Artis Paul, a lot of high notes, was one of Thomas Ross'.
I think he went up in Dakota with Trent.
He came here with Nat Towles briefly too. I think he did some writing.
But he let the whiskey get him.
